explanation: Count the two nodes’ depths using parent links. Lift the deeper node until depths agree, then lift both together until their references coincide.
timeComplexity: O(h): two depth scans, alignment and ascent each follow parent paths. C#/JavaScript may discover every node and store its parent; native callables already have parent links and only follow height-sized paths.
spaceComplexity: O(1): only depths and node cursors are kept. C#/JavaScript store parent entries for discovered nodes and an ancestor set; native code uses only two cursors and depths.
attribution: Unmodified EPIJudge reference source: epi_judge_java_solutions/epi/LowestCommonAncestorWithParent.java. Original contributors; repository LICENSE: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-nd/4.0/).
correctness: After depth alignment, both cursors are equally far below their common ancestors. Simultaneous parent steps preserve that equality, and the first shared reference is the lowest shared ancestor. Equal data alone is not used to identify a match.
walkthrough: In tree [6,2,9,1,4,8,12,null,null,3,5], node 5 is one level deeper than node 1. Lift 5 to 4, then lift 1 and 4 together to their common parent 2. Return node 2. JSON arguments are [tree,node0Data,node1Data]. C#/JavaScript receive those three arguments; native callables receive only the two resolved node references.
edgeCases: Inputs are existing nonnull nodes in the same tree with correct parent links.
A node is its own ancestor, so equal inputs return that node.
The wrapper resolves keys in a serialized tree and observes the returned node’s data.
